clue.text: Returned photo with woman's unreadable writing

indicators.note: returned means the short word for a photo is sent back, read from right to left

parts.note: a pic is an informal word for a photo
her is the possessive for a woman

explanation.surface: Someone gets back a snapshot along with a woman's illegible scrawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returned' turns PIC into CIP; HER follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A code turns a message into secret script that outsiders cannot read.

clue.text: I'm to get old, with lines in pictures

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
to age is to get old
RY, railway, gives the lines a train runs on

explanation.surface: Someone reflects on ageing as wrinkles appear in portraits.
explanation.walkthrough: RY (railway) is the crossword shorthand for lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Visual images collectively, in art or writing, form pictures.

clue.text: Hurry to accept a thousand, quite an increase

indicators.note: to accept means to take in, so the word for hurry surrounds the thousand

parts.note: hie is an old word meaning hurry
k stands for a thousand, as in kilo

explanation.surface: Someone rushes to take a big sum, quite a pay rise.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp rise in prices or wages is called a jump.

clue.text: Shoots animals over here for organ part

indicators.note: over says the whole run of shoots and animals is turned back to front

parts.note: pots as in pot-shots: to pot is to shoot
deer are animals

explanation.surface: A hunter shoots animals here, near the church organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses POTS DEER as a whole, giving REED STOP.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of pipes on a church instrument that sound with vibrating tongues is one of its stops.

clue.text: Installed Windows?

parts.note: reads like loading computer software, but means fitting panes of glass into window frames

explanation.definitionFit: A glazier fits glass into frames, so a building with its windows put in has been fitted with glass.

clue.text: Make tenuous expression of denial disheartening chap ?

indicators.note: disheartening means removing the heart, here the middle letter of the word for chap, with the denial put in its place

parts.note: a guy is a chap
'as if!' is a scornful expression of denial

explanation.surface: A dismissive phrase of refusal deflates a fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartening' takes the middle U out of GUY and puts AS IF in its place.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn something into vapour makes it thin and insubstantial, like a vapour.

clue.text: Associate's feat I fail to improve on

definitions.note: read as 'Associate is', the 's a link

indicators.note: to improve on means to rework, so the letters of feat, I and fail are rearranged

explanation.surface: A partner admits to a feat that he cannot better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to improve on' rearranges FEAT I FAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: To link up as a member or branch is to join or be connected with.

clue.text: They'll eliminate blunders (when first part of exercise is penned)

definitions.text: They'll eliminate blunders (when first part of exercise is penned)

parts.words: They'll eliminate blunders (when first part of exercise is penned)
parts.note: rubbers that wipe out mistakes, used once a schoolchild's first draft of an exercise has been written

explanation.walkthrough: The parenthesis is whimsical; the clue is a cryptic description of rubbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubbers wipe pencil marks, so they remove mistakes from written work.

clue.text: Class trek all over the place, lacking path

indicators.note: all over the place suggests disorder, so the letters of class trek are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A school party's hike goes chaotically, with no trail to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all over the place' rearranges CLASS TREK.
explanation.definitionFit: Land with no tracks across it has no path to follow.

clue.text: Sort of holiday giving one nightmares, perhaps?

indicators.note: perhaps hints the letters could be arranged differently

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A holiday arrangement keeps giving someone bad dreams.
explanation.definitionFit: A holiday home owned jointly, each owner using it for set weeks, is a shared-ownership vacation.

clue.text: Dishonesty shown by German woman and daughter

parts.note: Frau is the German for a woman or wife

explanation.surface: A German lady and her daughter are caught being deceitful.
explanation.definitionFit: Deception practised for gain is a criminal form of dishonesty.

clue.text: Bond entering service after detective's insight?

indicators.note: after places the bond and service run behind the detective

parts.note: DI, detective inspector, plus the possessive s

indicators.note: entering signals one piece going inside another, here the service inside the bond

parts.note: cement is a bonding agent
RN, the Royal Navy, is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: James Bond joins the service, following a detective's hunch.
explanation.walkthrough: RN (Royal Navy) goes inside CEMENT; 'Bond' is not 007 but a glue.
explanation.definitionFit: Keen judgement and perception amount to insight.

clue.text: Look stingy, by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says a word meaning stingy is spoken and a different spelling entered

parts.note: mean means stingy or miserly

explanation.surface: Someone's appearance seems miserly, or so it is said.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's bearing or facial expression is their look or demeanour.

clue.text: Treating us with flu, sense what's likely to help?

indicators.note: treating as in processing or working over, so the letters of us, flu and sense are reworked

explanation.surface: A doctor dealing with flu patients senses what might be helpful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Treating' rearranges US, FLU and SENSE; 'with' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: The quality of being of service is what makes something likely to help.

clue.text: Padre who guides TV company?

parts.note: Sky is a British satellite television company
a pilot is one who guides a ship or aircraft

explanation.surface: A chaplain is asked which person steers a television firm.
explanation.walkthrough: SKY is a British satellite TV broadcaster; a sky pilot is slang for a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: Sky pilot is slang for a clergyman, especially a military chaplain.

clue.text: Casually finishing popular drink, without taste?

indicators.note: finishing says the word for casually comes last

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable
to sip is to drink
idly means casually, without effort

explanation.surface: Someone lazily finishes a popular drink that has no flavour.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something blandly and dully is doing it with no flavour or zest.

clue.text: a church feature

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'a church feature (5)' appears cut short: no definition plus wordplay, and no scan to recover the missing words.

clue.text: See a divinity class changing in make-up

parts.note: v is short for vide, Latin for see
RI, religious instruction, is divinity as a school subject
a form is a school class

explanation.surface: A theology class is told to look at a change in its composition.
explanation.walkthrough: V (vide) means 'see'; RI is religious instruction, a school subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Having various forms means differing or changing in shape and composition.

clue.text: Hoard implying acknowledgement of foolishness?

definitions.meaning: to hoard is to gather and pile up a store
read as two words, saying 'I am an ass', admitting one is a fool

explanation.surface: Stockpiling things is taken as an admission of being silly.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into AM ASS and it confesses foolishness.
explanation.definitionFit: To accumulate and pile up goods is to hoard them; split, the letters also admit being a fool.

clue.text: Heather's following mother up country

indicators.note: following places the heather after the mother
up in a down entry means turned back, reading upward

parts.note: ma is mother
erica is the botanical name for heather; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: Heather trails behind her mother on a trip up country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns MA into AM; ERICA is the Latin name for heather.
explanation.definitionFit: The United States is a nation, often just called by this name.

clue.text: Note appropriate to county

parts.note: to appropriate is to take something for oneself
Down is a county of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A memo suits the local county council.
explanation.walkthrough: DOWN is a county in Northern Ireland. 'Note' is a verb: write down.
explanation.definitionFit: To write something down as a record is to jot it, as a secretary takes dictation.

clue.text: All right in a week on a Japanese island

parts.note: OK means all right

explanation.surface: Someone is fine spending a week on a Japanese island.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest of the Ryukyu chain lies south of Japan's main islands.

clue.text: Pacific islands where Idaho women will fill in a month?

indicators.note: fill in means go inside, so Idaho and women sit within the month

parts.note: May is a month
ID is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Idaho

explanation.surface: Women from Idaho will pass a spring month on islands in the Pacific.
explanation.definitionFit: The atoll was the site of a famous 1942 naval battle, in the middle of the Pacific Ocean.

clue.text: Sought-after export allowed? It's far from clear

parts.note: in means fashionable or in demand
exp is the standard abbreviation for export
licit means lawful or permitted

explanation.surface: A popular overseas shipment is permitted, though the rules are murky.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not stated plainly or directly is vague and unclear.

clue.text: Sentence in biography?

definitions.meaning: a prison term for the rest of one's days
an account of someone's days from birth onward

explanation.surface: A prison term turns up in someone's memoir.
explanation.definitionFit: A whole-of-days prison term and a written personal history share the same short word.

clue.text: Some frantic editors cooled down

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some harried newspaper editors finally calmed down.
explanation.definitionFit: Something chilled with frozen water has been cooled down.

clue.text: Crossword diagram involving new, tedious procedure

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the diagram word surrounds the letter for new

parts.note: a grid is the pattern of squares a crossword sits in

explanation.surface: Filling in a fresh crossword puzzle turns into a boring routine.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard, monotonous work is called a slog or drudgery.

clue.text: Try to win credit in silly exploitation of deal?

parts.note: to woo is to try to win someone's affections

indicators.note: in places the credit abbreviation inside the word for silly

parts.note: daft means silly

explanation.surface: Someone attempts to win credit with a foolish use of a business deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deal' is not a bargain but pine or fir timber, so using it well is skill with wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Skill in working timber makes good use of soft pine boards.

clue.text: Make superior fly out, keeping day free

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the reworked fly surrounds the reworked day
out as in disordered, so the three letters of fly are rearranged
free as in loosened, so the letters of day are set loose and rearranged

explanation.surface: A fly escapes, keeping the day clear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges FLY to LFY; 'free' rearranges DAY to ADY; 'keeping' puts ADY inside LFY.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise someone to genteel status is to make them a refined gentlewoman.

clue.text: Crazy block over agricultural policy?

indicators.note: over in a down-style reading means turned back, so the word for block reverses

parts.note: to dam is to block a flow
CAP is the EU's Common Agricultural Policy

explanation.surface: Farmers are wildly frustrated by a blockage in farm policy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns DAM into MAD; CAP is the EU's Common Agricultural Policy.
explanation.definitionFit: A reckless, impulsive person or scheme is wild and crazy.
